draft.title: Area of triangles and parallelograms
card: The base is one side of the shape. The perpendicular height is the straight distance from the base up to the opposite side, at a right angle to the base.
area = base × perpendicular height. The slanted side is not the height.
area = ½ × base × perpendicular height. It is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height.
Example: a triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².
draft.remember: Use the perpendicular height, never the slanted side. A triangle is half the base times height.

a.q: A parallelogram has base 8 cm, perpendicular height 5 cm and a slanted side of 6 cm. What is its area?
a.why: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm². Using the slanted side gives 48 cm², but the slanted side is not at right angles to the base.
a.clue: Which length is at a right angle to the base?

b.q: Zoe cuts a triangle of felt with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. What is its area?
b.why: Area = ½ × 12 × 7 = 42 cm². The answer 84 cm² forgets to halve, which gives the area of a parallelogram instead.
b.clue: A triangle is half of a parallelogram.

problems.detail: The card defines perpendicular height as the distance from the base 'up to the opposite side'. For a triangle, the height goes to the opposite vertex (corner), not a side. Students may be confused when applying it to triangles. Suggest 'to the opposite side or vertex'.

check.summary: Both answers check out (40 cm² and 42 cm²), and the distractors are good common errors. One small fix: the card's definition of perpendicular height says 'to the opposite side', which does not fit a triangle, where the height goes to the opposite corner.
